component.name: DrukhalManager
component.summary: Manage Stellaris mods and merge their conflicts

description.p: A native Linux mod manager for Stellaris that edits your load order, finds where mods conflict, and merges them into a patch so every mod's changes survive.
A fork of Irony Mod Manager by Mario (bcssov), rewritten in Rust with GTK and libadwaita.

ul.li: Edit the load order and keep several collections, synced to the Paradox Launcher
Find files and objects that several mods change
Merge conflicts with AI, or pick a version, into a patch mod
Repair files with brace mistakes and broken mod descriptors
See which mods caused the errors the game logged

description.p: Makes out-of-date merges easier to act on, reworks Fix with AI, and checks hand-made saves like AI merges:

ul.li: The object and game-update pages say why a saved merge is out of date and offer Keep As Is or Use New Version right there
The Needs Attention group stays current after saves and is found by searching for the merges it lists
Fix with AI can answer that an object is fine, offer alternatives, or list the lines it removed, and shows a before/after view to apply or keep
Fix with AI accepts replies from providers that send empty fields as null
Manual and whole-file saves get the same syntax, structure and duplicate-key checks as AI merges, without requiring every mod addition
The duplicate-key check allows repeats guarded by different conditions and identical copies, so valid game content isn't rejected

description.p: Fixes false "merge out of date" warnings after game updates, and hardens saving and AI requests:

ul.li: The saved-merge audit no longer counts values a mod copied from an older game version as dropped additions, so merges that keep the new game's values stay up to date
Base-game snapshots are ordered by game version, and the installed version's snapshot is never deleted after a rollback
Error-log fixes that fail validation are shown as rejected drafts and need "Use It Anyway" before saving
Hand-edited inline scripts are checked before they are saved
Patch files are never written outside the patch folder, and keys that clean up to the same name get separate files (8 terraform merges are renamed once)
The brace check handles escaped quotes, and localisation headers with a trailing comment are recognised
AI prompts tag mod text with a per-request marker, replies are size-capped, connections are reused, and Cancel stops a stalled reply at once
The out-of-date merge list is faster with large patches

description.p: Stops the saved-merge audit from flagging a script-value priority choice as a dropped addition:

ul.li: When the result keeps a current value: reference and an older mod used a different one, the audit now treats it as the merge's priority choice
Covers game updates that rename script values, such as value:count_assigned_priests replacing an older mod's value:country_assigned_priests
Clears old audit warnings for those merges without re-merging

description.p: Extends the saved-merge audit's equivalence rules so rewriting trigger blocks as flat conditions doesn't look like a dropped addition:

ul.li: Treats is_xenophobe = no and is_militarist = no as the same as NOR = { is_xenophobe = yes is_militarist = yes }
Ignores NOR/NOT block markers when comparing additions; their child conditions carry the meaning
Clears old audit warnings for merges that only changed how a negation is written

description.p: Stops the saved-merge audit from reporting equivalent ethic conditions as dropped additions:

ul.li: Treats is_pacifist, is_xenophile, is_xenophobe, and the other is_* ethic triggers as the same condition as the matching has_ethic pair
Treats a lone fanatic ethic as the matching is_fanatic_* trigger
Clears old audit warnings for merges that only rewrote one form as the other, without re-merging

description.p: Fixes merged events that inherit from another event and audits saved merges against their sources:

ul.li: Writes a merged event after the event it inherits from with base =, so the inheritance resolves and the event keeps is_triggered_only instead of firing every day
Moves existing patches saved with the old file name into place on the next check, without re-merging
Revalidates saved merges against their current sources and lists ones that dropped an addition, duplicated a single-valued key, or broke the script
Adds Keep As Is for those merges, so intentional edits are not reported again

description.p: Adds keyboard shortcuts across conflict resolution and dialogs, and fixes two inline-script merge bugs:

ul.li: Adds Alt+C for Copy This Over (copying the selection, highlighted difference, or cursor difference to the editable card) and Ctrl+Shift+F for Clean Up the Code
Adds Alt+S (Save to Patch), Alt+T (Take Change), Alt+Z (Undo Last Step), Alt+E (Open in Merge Tool), Ctrl+L (Look Up Objects), and lets Ctrl+F search Conflicts when on the Conflicts page
Adds Alt+M and Ctrl+S shortcuts to the File Merge, Fix, Folder Merge, and Inline Scripts dialogs, and lists all new shortcuts in the Keyboard Shortcuts window
Rewrites scalar inline_script = name calls alongside block calls when merging replaced inline scripts
Stages merged inline scripts in memory inside the File Merge dialog until Save is clicked, writing nothing on cancel

description.p: Avoids asking AI to rewrite objects when brace repairs are already unambiguous:

ul.li: Classifies mechanical brace repairs and only flags blocks closed before a new top-level object for AI review
Skips AI repair and enables saving directly when only stray closing braces were removed or blocks were closed at end of file
Resets the active-object tracker when brace depth returns to zero so stray braces aren't blamed on earlier objects

description.p: Keeps Fix with AI from dropping the content it is repairing:

ul.li: Rejects a brace repair that drops, alters or reorders any line, key, value or comment
Asks the model once more with the missing content when a repair is rejected
Leaves the editor untouched and reports the reason when the second repair is rejected too
Stops a repair as soon as Stop is pressed, including during the retry

description.p: Fixes saving a merged object when the result was opened after Merge All:

ul.li: Adds a Save to Patch button to the final result toolbar as well as the result card
Shows a toast and logs the save attempt, so a rejected or failed save is visible

description.p: Lets replaced inline scripts be merged or edited by hand, and trims API keys before use:

ul.li: Adds Merge with AI, an editable result, a target script name, and Save to Patch to the Inline Scripts comparison dialog
Stops the manual editor from being read-only when a replaced inline script needs a judgement call
Trims whitespace from saved, keyring and environment API keys before they are sent

description.p: Merges replaced inline scripts with their objects, and makes conflict merging safer:

ul.li: Detects when a mod replaces a vanilla inline script with its own copy, merges the script and the object together, saves it under the mod's script name, and rewrites the object's call to it
Updates replaced inline scripts during game updates when the vanilla script changed
Tracks merged inline scripts in the patch, removes them with their object or file, and keeps scripts shared by several merges
Gives AI merges the folder priority rule, the current winner, game version and replaced-script context; validates single-value keys, dropped additions, scripted variables and localisation files
Carries the missing source content into corrections instead of replaying the whole request
Adds AI result caching, model limits, request preflight, cancellation and cost reporting; retries transient provider errors and unsupported optional parameters

description.p: Inline script comparison, Omarchy theming, and smoother collection & conflict workflows:

ul.li: Adds side-by-side comparison for replaced or modified inline scripts in Object Conflicts and Game Update views
Advances to the next unresolved conflict when clicking Save to Merged Patch in Game Update and File Conflicts views
Adds live Omarchy desktop theme support (colors.toml and light.mode) for native and Flatpak builds
Preserves scroll position when enabling or adding mods so the mod list does not jump to the top
Shows the Missing Mods dialog on all collection imports (file, bundle, and clipboard), adds queued batch opening in browser, and auto-detects finished Steam Workshop downloads

description.p: Fixes false stale merge warnings and polishes game update conflict view:

ul.li: Tracks mod definitions moved between files across mod updates so merges are not falsely flagged as "no longer defines it"
Filters out contradictory stale merge warnings when a mod definition is actively loaded in the conflict view
Cleans up Game Update conflict detail view by removing duplicate buttons and redundant editable badges, compacting author report action, and ensuring all controls fit comfortably
Refines AI merge guidelines to prevent restoring blocks intentionally omitted by mods

description.p: Adds "Clean Up the Code" option to editor right-click menus:

ul.li: Formats spacing around operators (=, <, >, !=, <=, >=, ?=) and braces
Normalizes block nesting with clean tab indentation matching file context
Collapses excessive blank lines, removes trailing whitespace, and strips accidental semicolons
Cleans selected lines or the entire buffer, fully integrated with single-step undo

description.p: Updates scripting knowledge base and rules for Stellaris 4.6 (Corona Borealis):

ul.li: Teaches AI conflict merging and repair prompts new 4.6 renames, removals, and pop group rework patterns (every_owned_pop_group, kill_pop_group)
Adds knowledge of colony governor modifier renames, ethic pop-attraction mult updates, starbase waystation changes, and megastructure country scopes
Expands reference tables for 4.6 effects, triggers, modifiers, and script rules

description.p: Fixes a false-positive validator error on scripted effect and trigger definitions:

ul.li: Correctly distinguishes scripted effect and trigger definitions from scripted effect calls
Allows control flow blocks (if, switch, while) and scope changes inside scripted effect implementations without false undeclared parameter warnings
Continues guarding against invalid undeclared child blocks inside actual scripted effect calls

description.p: Added an agnostic collection export option compatible with Irony Mod Manager (and other cross-tool load orders):

ul.li: New "To an Irony Mod Manager File…" action in the Collections Export menu that generates a clean playset JSON
Provides explicit in-app guidance on importing into Irony Mod Manager via "Import from Paradox Launcher JSON"
Updated the collection file open filter to recognize Irony Mod Manager collections

description.p: Integrates "Changed by the Game Update" into the main Conflicts view:

ul.li: Replaced the standalone modal popup with a first-class "Changed by the Game Update" section directly in the Conflicts sidebar
Full support for search, filtering, and status tracking alongside other mod conflicts
Inline detail view with split diffs, manual edits, mod author bug report generator, external merge tool launcher, and AI update support
"Update All with AI…" action directly accessible from the section header menu

description.p: Redesigned Changed by the Game Update and improved diff copy behavior:

ul.li: Redesigned the Changed by the Game Update screen using a split view modeled after the conflict resolver, featuring a sidebar with object search, pills, notes, DiffBar controls, and an editable right card for instant manual and AI resolutions
Restored standard clipboard copy so Ctrl+C or right-click Copy no longer automatically mutates the right card
Added an explicit "Copy This Over" context menu item to copy selected or clicked differences to the editable card

description.p: Fixes a false "no longer defines it" warning for terraform link object merges (pc_from → pc_to) when checking patch freshness against mod copies and vanilla files.

Fixes a Stellaris 4.6 game startup crash (SIGSEGV in CScriptedEffect::visit) caused by invalid undeclared child blocks inside scripted effect calls. DrukhalManager now validates and prevents emitting undeclared child blocks inside scripted effects and scripted triggers in file-level and object-level merges. Also ensures diff cards and code views reset horizontal scrolling so text is never truncated on the left.

Outdated Game Objects: adds manual conflict resolution, external merge tool launching (3-way merge), quick reset buttons (Use Game's Version and Use Mod's Version), and a copyable "Report for Mod Author" bug report button. Also adds quick Merge File buttons for file and inline script conflicts, and ensures diff cards reset horizontal scroll so text is never shifted out of view.
Fixes CI lint warnings for whole-file AI merging.
Enables AI merging for overridden inline scripts and script fragments (such as common/inline_scripts/), combining distinct additions and triggers while preserving evaluation order.

Treats random_names and start_screen_messages as cumulative merged folders rather than individual conflicting objects, removing false conflicts and self-conflicts across empire name formats and intro screen message parts.
Fixes false conflicts and internal self-conflicts for random_list and terraform_link definitions across planet classes and terraforming scripts by resolving their inner unique names.
Fixes CI lint warnings and Windows test build portability.

Fixes conflict solver false conflicts for special projects and any other wrapped definitions using inner key attributes (e.g. special_project = { key = ... }), automatically extracting the inner unique key.

Invalidates the conflict scan cache so all mods are automatically re-indexed with the new inner-key object resolver, removing phantom conflict entries (ambient_object, message_type, ship_design, component_set, etc.) left over from previous cache versions.

Fixes conflict solver false conflicts for component sets, component templates, section templates, and ambient objects where definitions were grouped by block keyword rather than their inner unique key or name. Also introduces visual change indicators and bubbles in the Merged Result editor comparing the AI merge directly against the base game.

A Stop button now allows canceling in-flight AI Fix operations across script repair, game error, and brace fix dialogs immediately. Also resolves a conflict solver regression where ambient object definitions were mistakenly flagged as conflicting objects rather than coexisting file-level definitions.

Stellaris 4.6 compatibility: updated scripting rules and AI merge knowledge for the 4.6 "Corona Borealis" update, adding support for renamed district specialization keywords (included_buildings and excluded_buildings) and obsolete modifier replacements.

Script Performance: after running script_profiler twice in the game's console, a new sidebar link shows how much script time each enabled mod's objects took, slowest first, with each mod's slowest items. A mod that replaces the game's own scripts is credited with their time too. Outdated Merges and Merges to Check now have a Remove All button when they list more than one item; the patch is backed up first. The url dependency is updated for RUSTSEC-2026-0592.

Mods that change nothing: a new card in the health strip lists enabled mods whose every file is replaced by a mod loading later, with the mods that replace them, and turns them off with one click (undoable). In the conflict view, Ctrl+C on the view-only side still copies and now also takes every highlighted change the selection touches into the editable side, as one undo step. Big conflicts open faster with Changed Lines Only on, comparing again no longer recolours unchanged text, and scrolling no longer leaves seconds of work behind. Moving a mod in the load order now moves only its own row.

Fix problems by hand: Script Check's object pages and the Game Errors list now offer Edit by Hand next to Fix with AI. It opens the same side-by-side review starting from the mod's copy, so the problems can be corrected without an AI provider and saved to the merged patch. Saving still checks that the script parses and defines the object, and the row then says it's fixed in the patch.

AI requests now carry Model Instructions you can edit in Preferences → AI Merging. The default baseline tells the model to work from the text it was given, apply a rename or capitalisation fix directly, leave alone a problem that doesn't appear in the object, and decide once instead of restating the task or weighing options it can't check. It keeps the model's reasoning short, especially when a script problem refers to a name the shown definition doesn't contain. Reset to Default restores the baseline.

Safer settings and collections: a settings.json that can't be read is kept aside instead of being replaced by defaults, and the keyring migration no longer saves a stale copy over newer settings. Merged collections whose names make the same folder name now get a folder of their own instead of deleting each other, and replacing a merged folder can no longer leave neither the old nor the new one.

Hardening: zip extraction is capped in size and entry count and uses a unique temporary folder, so concurrent jobs can't share one; mod thumbnails can't point outside the mod or request huge images; Windows launch arguments keep their backslashes; a multiplayer report says which mod couldn't be unpacked instead of showing a false mismatch; and the external merge tool keeps non-UTF-8 output and warns when it exits at once without saving.

Smaller fixes: descriptor repair skips an unreadable descriptor instead of stopping, an old load-order backup that can't be deleted no longer blocks the save, crash-log paths with characters like Ω or İ no longer panic, frozen descriptors escape backslashes, AI object merges must define one object, and base-game snapshots have a format version and aren't saved after a read failure. The wiki now documents Script Check, “won by” ignore rules and the rule builder.

Script Check finds events that mods fire but nothing defines: an event call, an on_action events list or a random_events entry naming an event that neither the game nor an enabled mod has. A missing event in a namespace that exists is listed as a problem, and Fix with AI is told which events that namespace has. One whose namespace nothing installed has is listed under “Probably from another mod”.

Safer shared patches: a merged patch, or a patch bundle being imported, is refused if it names a file or folder outside the patch's own folder, so a malformed or malicious patch can no longer move or delete other files. Localisation merges only accept real language headers such as l_english, and a mod with a malformed header can no longer put a merged file outside the patch.

Ignore rules can be made by clicking. A new “won by” rule hides the conflicts in a folder while one mod's version is the one the game uses, such as a merger meant to override them, and shows them again if another mod overrides it. Add one from a folder's menu in the conflict list, from the menu beside Ignore Conflict, or with Add Rule. Each rule shows which conflicts it hides and which stay shown. The Ignore Rules dialog lists rules in words with a delete button, with the text editor behind Edit as Text.

Faster conflict scans: files the scan hasn't seen before are read on several threads, and each file is read once instead of once per object. The mod list, the error log's fixes and Look Up Objects also skip repeated work, so they respond faster with large mod lists.
Counts show as numbers again where they read “{count}”: the mods behind each conflict on the Conflicts page, a mod's conflicts in its details, and the number of compatibility patch suggestions.

A new look, in the style of Material 3. The interface uses the Google Sans Flex font, with Fira Code for scripts and Material Symbols icons, all bundled with the app. Buttons are pills, Launch and Sort Load Order are split pills, Load Order and Conflicts switch with a pill toggle, and the cards, panels and switches are rounded. Mods in the load order sit as separate tiles, and the selected one stands out. Colors still follow your desktop's accent and light or dark mode, including palettes from tools like DankMaterialShell and matugen.
Long links in the sidebar and long folder names on the Conflicts page now wrap instead of being cut off.

On the Conflicts page, conflicts saved to the merged patch move to a Resolved section at the bottom of the list, closed until you open it. Problems moves there too once every file with errors has a fix, instead of staying under Needs Attention. The list's headings are title-cased, and the mod filter now really reads Filter by Mod until you pick a mod.

Interface updates. The header's Collections button now always says Collections and marks the active one in its menu. The cards above the load order sit in rows of three, smaller, with the overview first and problems below. Search folds into an icon until you use it (or press Ctrl+F). Smart Sort is now Sort Load Order. In the sidebar, clicking a category jumps to its section and clicking its count shows only that section.

On the Conflicts page, the mod filter says Filter by Mod, the buttons under the list are even and labelled (Rules, Backups, Look Up, Rescan), ignoring a conflict is a labelled Ignore Conflict button, Merge with AI has a sparkle, and long titles, mod names and paths wrap instead of being cut off, with both versions' headers kept the same height. In Preferences, the version links to its release notes.

Game Errors recognises many more harmless lines and sorts them into their own collapsed groups (looks and sounds, missing text, references to other mods, mod descriptors, and more "defined twice"), so the problems list shows what can actually break the game. On a 158-mod log it went from about 18,000 problem lines to about 10,000.

Mods that only add an advanced authority swap to an existing authority (holding nothing but advanced_authority_swap blocks) are no longer shown as conflicting with each other, or as replacing the base game's authority, since the game adds their swaps instead.
The first conflict scan after updating re-reads every mod once.

Update All with AI. "Changed by the Game Update" can now bring every pending object up to date in one go. It asks first, with the number of requests and the estimated cost, then runs them without saving anything. You then review each result side by side and choose Save or Skip. The merged patch is backed up before the first save, and anything that failed is listed at the end so you can open it on its own.

Fix with AI in Game Errors now also works on objects a mod defines itself, which the base game doesn't have. It uses the game's script documentation as its reference, and rejects a fix that adds names the game doesn't have.

Script Check. A line on the Conflicts page now lists effects and triggers in your mods that the current game doesn't have. The game skips them without saying so, so the features they belong to quietly stop working. It checks against the script documentation the game writes each time it starts, so start Stellaris once after an update.
Fix with AI rewrites an affected object to what the current game uses, checks the result again, and lets you review it side by side before saving it to the merged patch.

Problems in scripted effects and triggers that nothing calls, less certain ones, and names that probably belong to another mod are sorted into their own collapsed sections and left out of the count, so the live problems come first.
Game Errors now treats an "Unexpected token" as harmless when the game simply removed that keyword, and says why.
Update with AI now knows about script names recent game versions renamed or removed, and points out keywords in its result that appear neither in your game nor in the mod's copy.

Fix errors with AI. When a real problem in Game Errors comes from a mod's outdated copy of a game object, Fix with AI rewrites that copy from the game's current version, keeping the mod's changes. You review it side by side, can edit it, and save it to the merged patch, which flags it again if the game or the mod changes. Any keyword in the result that appears neither in your game nor in the mod's copy is pointed out before you save.
Explain and Fix with AI now also know about script names recent game versions renamed or removed, from notes checked against the game's files.

Suggest improvements. Each real problem has a menu to suggest a note when an error names a keyword your game no longer has, or to report the error as harmless. It opens a pre-filled GitHub issue in your browser after showing you exactly what it contains, without your home folder; nothing is sent until you submit it there.

Find the real problems in the game's error log. Game Errors now shows real problems first, still grouped by mod, and collapses known-harmless messages into one line each with why they don't matter: unused modifiers, things defined twice, missing icons, and saved empire designs that use mods you've turned off. Errors that span several lines are read as one. The sidebar counts only real problems.

Explain asks your AI what a problem means, what it does in game and what to do about it, using the error, the mod's name, the game version and the lines of the mod's file around the error. Nothing is sent until you click it.

Smart Sort keeps mods where you put them. When you drag a mod or type a new position for it, Smart Sort now keeps it directly below the mod above it, and its preview says so. Choosing a section for the mod, or the Forget button in the Smart Sort preview, hands the decision back to Smart Sort.
In the Smart Sort preview, choosing a section for a mod now moves it right away, and Apply uses exactly the order shown.

Spot mods whose changes load order throws away. When two mods ship the same file, the game uses the copy from the one that loads last. After each conflict scan, a mod that loads above a bigger mod replacing most of its files gets a warning above the mod list, with a button to move it below that mod. Identical copies are ignored. Smart Sort now places such a mod directly below the mod it changes.
While dragging a mod, hold it near the top or bottom of the list to scroll.

Bring outdated mod copies up to date with AI. In the list of objects a game update changed under your mods, Update with AI applies the game's changes to the mod's copy and keeps the mod's own changes. You review the result side by side, can edit it, and save it to the merged patch, where it's checked again whenever the game or the mod changes.

See what a game update changed under your mods. When a mod replaces a technology, job, event or other object with its own copy and a Stellaris update then changes that object, the mod keeps loading its old copy and the game's change doesn't apply. After an update, a line above the Conflicts list now counts these objects, and each one shows what the game changed side by side.

This works from the next Stellaris update after you install this version: DrukhalManager keeps a compressed copy of the base game's objects (about 3.5 MB per version, the last three versions) the first time it scans each version.
Look up any object. The new search button under the Conflicts list finds which of your mods define an object, event or localisation key, even when only one mod does, and which version the game uses.

Fewer false conflicts. Mods that pull in an inline script were sometimes shown as conflicting over an object called "inline_script", which doesn't exist. The first conflict scan after this update reads your mods' files again, once.

Faster conflict scans after updates. What a scan learns from reading your mods' files is now kept when DrukhalManager updates, so the first scan after an update no longer reads every file again. This takes effect from the update after this one.
Under the hood. Updated libraries, including the bundled SQLite and, on Windows, the code that keeps API keys in Credential Manager. Keys you saved before are still found.

A faster load order. Dragging, toggling, sorting, undoing and redoing no longer rebuild every row of the list, only the ones that changed. With a few hundred mods, moving one mod is about five times faster, and sorting about twice as fast.
Opens sooner with zipped mods. Mods that come as zip files are unpacked in the background after the window opens, instead of before it.

Quicker merged patch checks. Checking whether merges are out of date reads each mod and game file once, instead of once per merge. With a large merged patch this takes milliseconds instead of a noticeable pause at startup and after every scan.
Smaller download. The app itself is about a fifth smaller.

DrukhalManager 1.0, now on Windows. The same app, with the same interface, runs on 64-bit Windows. Download DrukhalManager-setup-x64.exe from the release to install it, or the zip to run it without installing. The downloads aren't code-signed yet, so the first time Windows SmartScreen asks: click More info, then Run anyway.

Change several mods at once. Ctrl+click and Shift+click select mods in either list. A bar under the list enables or disables them, moves them to the top or bottom, sets their category or adds them to another collection, each as one undo step. While a view, a category or a search narrows the list, Select All Shown selects every mod in it.

Mod updates since you last played. A card in the health strip lists the mods Steam updated since your last launch, with links to their change notes, and offers to freeze the collection. Another card lists Workshop updates Steam hasn't downloaded yet.

Find compatibility patches. Find More… on the Compatibility Patches section asks Steam which Workshop items need your enabled mods, and suggests the patches that fit your load order. It needs a Steam Web API key in Preferences.
Picked versions stay current. When you chose Use This Version and that mod later changes the object while nothing else does, Outdated Merges offers Use New Version instead of a new merge.
Merged patch in the Extra Mod Folder. A collection's menu can move its merged patch to the Extra Mod Folder, and back.

A shorter main menu. It keeps Preferences, Keyboard Shortcuts, Troubleshooting and About. The rest sits next to what it acts on: Undo, Redo and Reload in the header; Saves, Multiplayer Check, DLC and Find the Crashing Mod under Launch; Merged Patch Backups at the bottom of the Conflicts list.
Fixes. DrukhalManager opens before the game's first start, with no mods listed, instead of stopping at "Could Not Read Mods".

Notifications in one place. A bell in the header keeps every notification, newest first, with its time and its button, such as Show or Restart. Dismiss them one by one, or all at once with Clear All. Repeats are folded into one, and a badge counts the new ones. Toasts no longer stay on screen until closed.

Notes on mods. Write yourself a note on any mod, such as why it sits where it does, from its menu. The note shows as an icon on the row and in the mod's details, where you can edit it in place. Search finds notes, and a shared collection file can carry them.

Diagnostics for bug reports. DrukhalManager now keeps a small log of scans, merged patch changes, AI calls, game sessions and update checks. It never holds API keys, prompts or file contents. Main Menu, then Troubleshooting, copies a report to paste into a bug report or opens the log folder.

Categories in the Load Order. The sidebar lists the Smart Sort categories with how many mods each holds; click one to see only its mods. The load order shows a small header wherever the category changes, and says when mods were moved there by hand. Turn the headers off in the Smart Sort menu.
Faster conflict scans. Scans remember what they read, so a rescan only reads the files that changed, even after restarting the app.
Fixes. The Conflicts page no longer freezes for a few seconds after a scan or while searching.
Changed Lines Only. A new toggle on the Conflicts page folds the lines that are the same in both versions, keeping a few around each difference. Click a fold to open it.
Put This In. Right-click a difference on the view-only version to copy those lines into the version you're editing.

Keyboard shortcuts for conflicts. Alt+Page Down and Alt+Page Up move between conflicts, Alt+Left and Alt+Right use the left or right version, Alt+M merges with AI and Alt+I ignores a conflict. They're listed in Keyboard Shortcuts.
Choose the Claude model. Preferences → AI Merging lets you pick which Claude model merges, with its price, and cost estimates follow your choice.
Fixes. Preferences now says whether your API keys are in the system keyring or, when there is none, in DrukhalManager's own settings file. A Steam Web API key can be saved without a keyring.

One merged patch per collection. Merges only fit the load order they were made for, so each collection now has its own merged patch, named after it, and switching collections switches patches. The patch you had becomes the active collection's. Backups, exporting with the patch and importing work per collection: an imported patch goes to the new collection instead of replacing yours.

Freeze a collection. Freeze This Collection…, in the collection menu, copies its Workshop mods into local mods, so Steam updating one can't break a campaign in progress. The health strip shows when Steam has newer versions, and Unfreeze switches back to the Workshop mods and deletes the copies.
Merge Tool… for whole files. Overridden text files on the Conflicts page, and the file merge dialog, can be merged in Meld, KDiff3, VS Code or another tool too.

Multiplayer check. The report says whether you run the native Linux build or the Windows one, as players report that their checksums never match. Comparing reports now points out files that differ only in line endings, and files the native Linux build may skip because of how their names are capitalised.
Smoother Preferences. Preferences is split into Game, Merging, AI Merging, Steam and Updates pages, and opens without stuttering. The Conflicts page fits narrower windows.

A redesigned load order. A health strip above the list shows what needs attention: mods not updated for the game, required mods that are missing, mods loading before ones they need, out-of-date merges and achievements, each with a button to show or fix it. A sidebar of views lists the mods that need attention, aren't updated, have conflicts, turn off achievements or are disabled. Rows take one line each, and selecting a mod shows its problems, needs and actions in a panel beside the list.

Workshop required items. With your own Steam Web API key, set in Preferences, mods' Workshop “Required items” are checked like dependencies: missing, disabled or late ones are pointed out, sorting puts them first, and Get Required Mods enables or opens them. Items that aren't really mods, such as “Stellaris 101: How to Read”, are left out, and any other can be dismissed.
Mods not updated yet. After a game update, DrukhalManager lists the enabled mods that don't support the new version yet, and can set them aside in a collection until they do.

Campaigns remember their mods. Each campaign remembers the mods it was played with. Launching it with different mods asks first, and offers to switch back to its collection. Saves… lists campaigns and their mods.
Find the Crashing Mod… narrows down the mod that crashes the game by halving the enabled mods between launches, keeping dependencies together, and puts your load order back at the end.
Fixes. Messages no longer go blank when a name contains “&”, and long ones wrap.
Merge into One Mod can write the merged mod as one zip file, and can write it to an extra mod folder.
An Extra Mod Folder, in Preferences, lists and loads the mods kept in it, such as local mods on another drive or in a git checkout.
Export with the Merged Patch saves a collection together with its merged patch in one zip. Importing it installs the patch, after backing up yours.
The multiplayer report can include all the game's files, to find modified or damaged ones outside the multiplayer checksum. Repeated reports are faster, as file hashes are remembered.

Merge Tool… on the Conflicts page opens two versions of a definition in Meld, KDiff3, VS Code or another tool set in Preferences, and uses what you save. The Flatpak needs a one-time permission for it, which the app explains.

The mod search understands filters: enabled:, source:, achievements:, conflicts: and version:, with -- to leave mods out, || for either, and quoted phrases. It also finds mods by Workshop ID. The Filters button next to the search box sets them for you.

Collections can be imported from the game's current load order and from Paradox Launcher playset files, and exported as a playset file for players who use the launcher. Import and export are now submenus of the collection menu.
The name Merge into One Mod gives the merged mod can be chosen in Preferences, with {Name} for the collection's name.
Overridden images, including DDS textures, are shown side by side on the Conflicts page with their sizes, and Use This Version puts the chosen copy in the merged patch.

Copy Load Order and Paste Load Order, in the collection menu, share a load order as a numbered list with Workshop links, ready for a chat or forum post. Pasting one, or a collection file, makes a new collection.
Mods can be renamed with names only DrukhalManager shows, such as "UIOD" for a long Workshop title. Search finds both names.
A collection keeps the mods it lists that aren't installed, under Not Installed, with a Workshop link. When one is installed and the mods are reloaded, it goes back into its place.
DLC… in the main menu turns DLCs on and off.
The Disabled list can be sorted by name or by when mods were last updated.
Include Test Versions, in Preferences, offers betas and release candidates as well.

Smart Sort arranges the load order the way the Stellaris community's guides suggest: unofficial patches first, then graphics, flavor, shipsets, galaxy generation, gameplay and large overhauls, compatibility patches, UI mods and their patches, and universal patches last. Sub-mods go directly below the mod they need, and every mod still loads after its dependencies. A preview shows where each mod goes and why, and any mod can be moved to another section; the choice is remembered.
Sort A–Z, Dependencies First sorts the load order by name while keeping mods after their dependencies.
Merge All now works on folders of overridden files too, with one AI call per object the copies disagree on.
Text boxes, such as the AI's reasoning, merged results and the file editors, can be resized by dragging the grip below them.

After a Stellaris update, merges are checked against the new game too: ones whose objects or files the base game has added since are flagged as outdated, base-game definitions that moved to another file are followed instead of reported missing, and the reasons name the update.

The merged patch is backed up before each Merge All and before merges are removed. Merged Patch Backups in the main menu restores any of the last ten, so a batch merge that went wrong can be undone in one step.
The Flatpak now applies custom libadwaita colour schemes from ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css, such as DankMaterialShell's or matugen's, and picks up a new palette while it's open.
When an update needs a new Flatpak permission, which the app can't install itself, it says how to update instead.

Choose which localisation languages the conflict scan reads, in Preferences under Game. It defaults to the game's language, so translations you don't play in no longer show up as conflicts, and localisation can be left out of the scan altogether.
The Flatpak applies custom libadwaita colour schemes from your GTK 4 stylesheet.

Conflicts between a mod and the mods it depends on, such as a compatibility patch and the mods it patches, are hidden, since the patch is meant to override them. Show them again from Rules… on the Conflicts page.
When an AI merge comes back broken, the error goes back to the model once for a corrected version before the merge counts as failed.
Merge All can merge several objects at once; set how many in Preferences. Merges wait and try again when the provider is rate limited.

Ignore rules: hide conflicts by path, such as gfx/** or localisation/*, optionally only for an exact set of mods. Open them with Rules… on the Conflicts page, which previews how many conflicts each rule hides.
The mod list marks Workshop mods with an update Steam hasn't finished downloading, mods still downloading, and mods you unsubscribed from.
The Conflicts page shows which mod's version the game uses today, and why: file names, the folder's rule, or the load order.
Fixed merges in some folders, such as scripted variables and component templates, being ignored by the game. Merges already saved there are moved to the right place.
The Conflicts page has a new look: conflicts are listed in a sidebar, and each one shows the two versions side by side with the differences highlighted.
The later-loading version can be edited by hand before you use it, and your edits can be undone.

More mod thumbnails show up: mods without a picture in their descriptor use their thumbnail.png, file names match whatever their capitalisation, and Workshop mods with no image on disk show their Workshop preview.
The merged patch is marked with the app's icon.
Fixed the conflict scan failing when a mod has files with non-English characters in their names.
A failed scan now shows what went wrong.

Conflicts that need no AI, because only one mod changed the object from the base game or every mod ships the same version, are marked on the Conflicts page. Merge All saves them directly, without calls or cost, and the merge dialog fills in the version to use.
Workshop mods have new menu items: Open in Steam, Open Workshop Page in Browser, Copy Workshop Link and Unsubscribe in Steam.
Looking up the base game's versions of many objects is much faster.

Merge All merges every conflicting object in a folder with AI. It shows the number of calls and an estimated cost first, streams the model's thinking under each object, lets you view each merged result, and reports the tokens and cost actually used.
Workshop mods downloaded by Steam now appear without starting the Paradox Launcher, and updated mods show their new name and version.
Reload Mods (F5 or Ctrl+R) picks up mods subscribed, updated or removed while the app is open, keeping the load order.
Steam Workshop collections can be imported as a collection, with links to subscribe to any mods that are missing.
A whole collection can be merged into one mod.
Localisation files that hold several languages can now be merged.
Interface (.gui) and graphics (.gfx) files can now be merged object by object, as can files that repeat one kind of object, such as ambient objects or font overrides.
The Conflicts page can be filtered to one mod, and Show Conflicts in a mod's menu opens it filtered.
Inline scripts are no longer reported as conflicting objects.
Mods that turn off achievements are marked in the load order, and the status line says whether your collection keeps them.
The Launch button's menu can continue your last save directly.
Mods show their thumbnails in the load order.
New Multiplayer Check in the main menu: save a report of your game and mods to send to the other players, or open theirs to see which mods, files, versions or load order differ.
API keys are now kept in your system keyring instead of the settings file; a key saved earlier moves there the next time you start DrukhalManager.
Press ? or Ctrl+? (or use the main menu) to see the keyboard shortcuts.
Zipped mods are now scanned for conflicts and can be merged like any other mod.
Merges saved by versions before 0.1.0 are listed on the Conflicts page so you can check them; keeping one makes DrukhalManager notice when its mods change.
Installing an update from inside the Flatpak works; before, clicking Update did nothing. On desktops where Flatpak can't ask whether the app may update itself, DrukhalManager now says so.
The Flatpak now points out errors Stellaris logged about your mods after you play, as the native build does, and both say when the game crashed.
Preferences explain why the game executable can't be changed in the Flatpak.
Preferences now cover the game: choose the executable and data directory, add launch options, refresh mod descriptors before playing, and close after launching.
DrukhalManager shows its version in About and Preferences, tells you when a new version is out, and in the Flatpak installs it and restarts into it.
Undo and redo for the load order (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z). The Flatpak now updates itself through its own signed repository.
First release: load order editing and collections, conflict detection, AI-assisted merging into a patch mod, file repair, load order checks and game error reports.
